name: Uninstall detection through push failures
plain: Servers learn an app was removed when the push provider reports the token as invalid.
meaning: A company can tell, days later, which people deleted the app and then retarget them in ads or email. No on-device code runs after uninstall; the signal is the push service reply.

android.persistence: Visible to the server days after removal; FCM returns UNREGISTERED or NOT_FOUND once a send fails
android.store_policy: No Play rule forbids detecting churn; privacy policy must disclose
android.note: Detection is not instant: the Play services connection must report the removal; typical delay hours to days

ios.persistence: APNs returns 410 Unregistered with a timestamp once the token is invalid
ios.note: Apple says a 410 is returned after the app is removed; the old feedback service was retired (2021)

limits.headline: Can find out the app was removed, but only after hours or days
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app's server learns it when a push fails
can: Learn the app was removed when the push service says the token is invalid
Stop sending messages to that device
Mark you as inactive in its records
cannot: Know right away; Android can take hours to days
Get a direct feedback service from Apple, which was retired in 2021
Learn anything about the phone after you remove it
limits.reach_label: A late hint that you removed it
limits.differs: On iPhone, Apple returns a 410 error after removal. On Android, the delay depends on Google Play services.

story.what_it_is: Companies can tell later that you deleted their app because their push messages stop working.
story.for_you: You never notice. After you delete an app, the company may learn a day or more later that you left. You may then get email or ads trying to win you back.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to measure churn and run win back campaigns. It is quiet, cheap and works because the push service tells the server the address is dead.

use_cases.example: A product team charts how many people deleted the app after each update.
A marketer sends a win back ad to someone who just uninstalled a shopping app.
A game studio spots players who quit after level 5 and sends a come back offer by email.
A store sees an uninstall and moves you to an email only plan.
A streaming service learns viewers left and tries a free month offer.
A bank sees that a registered phone no longer has the app and may flag the device as gone.
Measurement tools like Firebase and AppsFlyer report uninstall counts to teams.

story.android_note: Detection can lag hours to days because it relies on Play services.
story.ios_note: Apple returns an error code once the app is removed. The old feedback service was retired in 2021.

technical_bounds: Only a server inference; no device event
Can be a false positive if the token rotated

abuse: Retargeting people who deleted the app

history.change: Binary Feedback Service retired; 410 responses are the signal
Legacy API errors replaced by HTTP v1 error codes
